answer.held_back_by: Honesty, I think. The card says my blunt Y27 answer removed my ceiling, so being straight apparently capped me even though my appraisals always said strong. I also never got an invitation into politics, so maybe visibility mattered more than integrity.
answer.ending_fair_why: I only learned on the final card that one choice at 27 shut my ceiling, and nothing during the run told me that. I was also left with the drawer letter, the stretch assignment, the 'game' joke and the different-life invite all unresolved. The 85 exposure line is weird too, because I retired at 65 and it never says what surfaces.
answer.chase_next: The politics ending, the 'different life'. I'd lie and play the visibility game to see if the invitation ever comes, since I never got to see what was past Permanent Secretary.
answer.play_again_why: The early and middle years had good hooks, but the late game coasted and left most of my threads dangling. I'd want to know what pays off before spending another life on it.

tone_breaks.note: I retired at 65 and the game never showed my life past that point, so it reads like a threat without a payoff.

tone_breaks.line: No street is named after you and none ever will be, which is rather the point.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about grades, appraisals and holding a post, not the pay, and the 'Confirmed' idea of being assessed is what drove everything. Minister Salary suggests politics, which I never reached.
